title_en: The Islamic Religious Sciences — Tape Eleven
body_ar:
فرجعت إلى كتب المؤلفين في بعض القصص المفيدة، التي يمكن تنزيلها على الواقع وأخذ الأحكام منها، تجد ما ينقل فيها عن الصحابة هو من رواية أبي مخلف ونوح بن أبي مريم ونحوهم من الذين لا يمكن أن تقبل روايتهم، ولذلك فمن العجيب أن محمد بن جرير الطبري على إمامته وجلالة قدره من أئمة أهل السنة اعتمد في نقل آثار علي رضي الله عنه في قضية الفتنة وآثارها عن طلحة والزبير وعائشة على أبي مخلف، وكذلك الحافظ بن كثير وابن الأثير في الكامل وغيرهم من كبار الأئمة المؤرخين، لا يوجد بديل.

بالنسبة لكتاب العواصم من القواصم لأبي بكر بن العربي لم يكن موثقا بالنقول، وإنما كانت استنباطات وآراء، وأكثر ما فيه طعون في النقول السابقة، هو بمثابة الرد، مثلا تنقل قصة عن الوليد بن يزيد بن عبد الملك، فيأتي هو فيكر عليها حتى يبطلها من ناحية الإسناد مثلا، لكن هذا لا يكفي أين البديل، تاريخهم ليس مجهولا وهو تاريخ عصر كبير من أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، أين ذهب هذا الذي نفقده حتى الآن مع الأسف، حتى في ردود شيخ الإسلام ابن تيمية على الشيعة في منهاج السنة واضح جدا فيه أنه يفقد النقول الكافية فيما يتعلق بقضية ما جرى بين الصحابة، ولذلك ففي بعض المواقف يتشدد هو حتى يكون لازم قوله مخالفا لمذهبه، ولا يقصد ذلك، لا يقصد النصب أعاذه الله من ذلك، لكن يفهم من كلامه في بعض الأحيان رأي النواصب، وإنما ذلك تحمسا واندفاعا في الرد...

أما ما يتعلق بالفرق الإسلامية وجمع عقائدها فقد ألف فيه عدد من المؤلفات من أهمها كتاب الفصل في الملل والنحل لأبي محمد علي بن حزم الأندلسي، وكذلك كتاب الملل والنحل للشهرستاني، وكتاب الفرق للبغداد، وقد ذكرنا أن أبا الحسن الأشعري في كتابه مقالات الإسلاميين أتى على أهم الفرق الموجودة في زمانه، وقد جاء ابن الجوزي أيضا في كتابه تلبيس إبليس ببعض أقوال الفرق، وقد توسع الناس في الكلام في الفرق حتى أدخلوا أديانا من الأديان التي هي خارج الإسلام أصلا، وما ذلك إلا أنهم درسوا مذاهب بعض الفرق المنحرفة التي كفر أصحابها، فلما كان هؤلاء وإن كانوا يدعون النسبة إلى هذه الأمة ليسوا منها وليسوا من المصدقين بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم توسع الناس في البحث فأتوا بالمذاهب اليهودية والنصرانية، المذاهب المنحرفة عموما في أشكال الانحراف، وذلك حين توسعوا في دراسة مذاهب الشيعة ودراسة مذاهب الخوارج ودراسة مذاهب الصوفية الغلاة، وهذه الطوائف الثلاثة لديها بعض المعتقدات المأخوذة عن الملل الأخرى غير الإسلام، ولهذا طورت حتى أصبحت ديانات مستقلة، كالسيخية الآن التي هي دين مستقل من أديان الهند الذين ينتحلونه في الأصل كان أجدادهم من المسلمين، كانوا طائفة صوفية ثم انحرفوا، وكذلك الدروز كانوا شيعة، وهكذا، فكثير من الطوائف التي بدلت دينها بالكلية كانت في الأصل داخل الملة الإسلامية ثم خرجت منه بالانحراف خرجت من الملة الإسلامية بالانحراف، فهذا الذي أحوج إلى الكتابة في هذا المجال.

ولهذا من المستحسن جدا أن يركز على المسائل المهمة في زيادة الإيمان التي تزيد القرب من الله سبحانه وتعالى وتزيد التعبد له والعناية بشرعه، بدل التركيز على المسائل العقيمة التي كثير منها لو جهله الإنسان وأتى يوم القيامة وهو يجهله لم يكن في ذلك نقص عليه، ولذلك فرد المصيصية على أحمد بن أبي دؤاد كان بليغا، فأحمد بن أبي دؤاد مكث فترة طويلة أربعين سنة وهو يناظر أهل العلم، وما استطاع أحد منهم أن يكسره، وأتي بكبار العلماء من أمثال الإمام أحمد بن حنبل وغيرهم من الأئمة الكبار، لكن كانوا يناظرونه ويجادلونه بالنقل، ما عندهم إلا أقوال عمن سلف حدثنا فلان قال: أخبرنا فلان، وهو لا يعترف بهذا، حتى جاء المصيصي فسأله فقط سؤالين، السؤال الأول قال: أرأيتك هذا الذي تدعو إليه أشيء عرفه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأبو بكر وعمر وعثمان وعلي أم جهلوه، قال: بل عرفوه، قال: أفدعوا الناس إليه هذا السؤال الثاني: أدعوا الناس إليه أم لا أم سكتوا عنه؟ قال: بل سكتوا عنه، قال: شيء عرفه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأبو بكر وعمر وعثمان وعلي فسكتوا عنه جدير بك أن تسكت عنه، فقال: أقلني والمسألة على حالها، بل جهلوه، قال: شيء جهله رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأبو بكر وعمر وعثمان وعلي من أين لك علمه؟ فالسؤال هنا عن سبب انتشار المذهب الأشعري في العالم الإسلامي، أقول إن المذهب الأشعري هو أقدم مذاهب أهل السنة، فالأقدمية لها اعتبار، ثم بعد ذلك أنه مذهب أكثرهم فلم يكن مختصا بمذهب من المذاهب الفقهية بل فيه حنابلة وفيه شافعية وفيه مالكية وفيه حنفية، بخلاف المذهب الماتريدي فمختص بعلماء الحنفية، والمذهب الحنبلي فمختص بالحنابلة في ذلك الزمان أو أهل الحديث معهم، فهذا السبب الأساسي من أسباب انتشاره، لكن الذي انتشر مع الأسف في الأخير في أكثر البلدان ليس هو مذهب الأشعري بل هو الأقوال التي طور إليها مذهب الأشعري وذكرنا أن بداية تطويره كانت مع الفخر الرازي.

أما ما يتعلق بالفرق المعاصرة وبالأخص الروافض وكذلك الإباضية التي ابتلي بها بعض البلدان كيف التعامل مع هؤلاء هل بالكبت وكتمان أنفاس هذا المذهب حتى يذهب أو بمجادلتهم ومناظرتهم أقول إن للسلف في هذا مذاهب شتى، فمنهم من كان يتسع باله لمناقشة أهل الزيغ والإلحاد لعل الله أن يهديهم أو على الأقل يقيم الحجة عليهم

يأبى الجواب فما يكلم هيبة *** شرف الوقار وعز سلطان التقى

وحتى في الحديث إذا بلغ حديثا أي قال أنه بلغه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، لم يستطع أحد أن يسأله عن إسناده فيه، يذكر أنه مرة واحدة سأله شعبة بن الحجاج قال: ممن سمعت هذا يا أبا عبد الله؟ قال: ما جالست سفيها قط ولم يجبه، لأنه لا يروي إلا عن الثقات عنده، لكن من مذاهبهم أيضا التفريق بين من يرجى رجوعه وهو من يصلح للدعوة مثل عوام الناس الذين يقلدون أهل الأخطاء في انحرافاتهم وأخطائهم وبين من لا يرجى رجوعه، فمن لا يرجى رجوعه بالنسبة لمعاملتهم فيما سوى ذلك هي مثل مخالطة الجار أيا كان فالجار المسلم له حقان والجار غير المسلم له حق واحد، فلذلك كما صرح بذلك النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فمن كنت تكفره منهم كالذي يرمي عائشة رضي الله عنها بما برأها الله منه ويعلن ذلك فهو كافر فأنت تكفره صراحة بما قال، وتعامله معاملة الجار الكافر، لأنه وإن كان ليس مثل الكافر الأصلي فهو كافر مرتد لكن لا تستطيع إقامة الحد عليه الآن وليس بيدك ذلك فتجعله كالكافر الأصلي، وبالأخص إذا كان نشأ على هذا قبل بلوغه، فليس هو بالمرتد لأنه وجد آباءه على هذا.

بالنسبة لرد السلام على الكفرة منهم، لا ترد عليه السلام ولا تبدؤه بالسلام، ومن كنت لا تكفره كعوامهم فتبتدئه بالسلام وترد عليه السلام، أما معاملتهم في العمل فلا يحل ظلمهم، الظلم محرم في جميع الشرائع، لا يحل ظلم اليهودي ولا ظلم النصراني ولا ظلم الرافضي ولا ظلم المنحرف في أي ملة من الملل، فإذا كان تلميذا فلا يحل لك أن تهضم شيئا من حقه إن استحقه في الامتحان، وإذا كان عاملا أو موظفا لا يحل لك هضم شيء من حقه، فالظلم ظلمات يوم القيامة، والله تعالى يقول حتى في حق المشركين الأصليين.

ففي معاملة المسلمين للكفار دائما كثير من التعامل الدعوي الذي أثر في نفسياتهم وجعل كثيرا منهم يسلمون وينقادون، حتى مع اليهود لا يظلمون لكنهم في قتالهم وظلمهم فيما ظلموا فيه يرد عليهم ظلمهم ويقتلون بما قتلوا به، لكن بالنسبة لمن كان لديه أمانة أو نحو ذلك يؤديها إليهم كما فعل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حين ظلمه أهل مكة وأخرجوه بغيا عدوانا وكذبوه أدى إليهم أماناتهم جميعا، ترك عليا يؤدي إليهم أماناتهم.
body_en:
So I went back to the books of the authors for some of the useful accounts — those that can be brought to bear on present reality and from which rulings can be drawn. You find that what is transmitted in them from the Companions comes by way of the narration of Abu Mikhlaf, Nuh ibn Abi Maryam and others like them, whose narration cannot possibly be accepted. And so it is astonishing that Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari — for all his standing as an imam and the eminence of his rank among the leading authorities of the people of the sunnah — relied, in transmitting the reports of Ali (may God be pleased with him) on the matter of the civil strife, and its reports from Talhah, al-Zubayr and Aisha, upon Abu Mikhlaf; and likewise al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir, and Ibn al-Athir in al-Kamil, and others among the great authorities among the historians. There is no alternative to be had.

As for the book al-ʿAwāṣim min al-Qawāṣim of Abu Bakr ibn al-Arabi, it was not documented with transmitted reports; rather it consisted of inferences and opinions, and most of what is in it consists of impugnments of the earlier transmissions. It stands as a refutation. For example, a story is transmitted about al-Walid ibn Yazid ibn Abd al-Malik, and he comes and turns upon it until he invalidates it from the side of the chain of transmission (isnād), say. But this is not enough — where is the alternative? Their history is not unknown, and it is the history of a great age of the community of Muhammad (may God bless him and grant him peace). Where has it gone, this which we lack to this day, regrettably? Even in the refutations of Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah against the Shia in Minhāj al-Sunnah, it is very clear in it that he lacks sufficient transmitted material on the question of what took place between the Companions. And for that reason, in some places he takes so severe a line that the necessary implication of his statement comes out contrary to his own position — and he does not intend that. He does not intend hostility to Ali and his house (naṣb); may God protect him from that. But what is understood from his words, at some times, is the view of the Nawasib; and that is only out of zeal and impetuosity in refutation…

As for what concerns the Islamic sects and the gathering of their creeds, a number of works have been composed on it. Among the most important of them is the book al-Faṣl fī al-Milal wa-l-Niḥal of Abu Muhammad Ali ibn Hazm al-Andalusi; likewise the book al-Milal wa-l-Niḥal of al-Shahrastani; and the book al-Farq of al-Baghdad[i]. We have mentioned that Abu al-Hasan al-Ash'ari, in his book Maqālāt al-Islāmiyyīn, covered the most important of the sects existing in his time; and Ibn al-Jawzi too, in his book Talbīs Iblīs, brought forward some of the statements of the sects. People went to great lengths in discussing the sects, until they brought in religions that are outside Islam altogether. The reason for that is simply that they studied the schools of certain deviant sects whose adherents were declared to be unbelievers; and since these people — even though they claim affiliation to this community — are not of it and are not among those who hold the Prophet (may God bless him and grant him peace) to be truthful, people went to great lengths in their investigation and brought in the Jewish and the Christian schools, and the deviant schools generally, in the various forms of deviation. That was when they went to great lengths in studying the schools of the Shia, and studying the schools of the Kharijites, and studying the schools of the extremist Sufis. These three groups have certain beliefs taken from religious communities other than Islam, and for this reason they developed until they became independent religions — such as Sikhism today, which is an independent religion among the religions of India; those who profess it, their forefathers were originally Muslims: they were a Sufi group, and then they deviated. Likewise the Druze were Shia, and so on. Many of the groups that changed their religion entirely were originally within the Muslim religious community and then went out of it through deviation — they went out of the Muslim religious community through deviation. This is what created the need for writing in this field.

For this reason it is very much to be commended that one concentrate on the important questions bearing on the increase of faith (īmān) — those that increase nearness to God, glorified and exalted, and increase devotion to Him and attention to His law — instead of concentrating on the sterile questions, many of which, if a person were ignorant of them and came on the Day of Resurrection still ignorant of them, that would be no deficiency in him. And for that reason the reply of al-Misisi to Ahmad ibn Abi Du'ad was telling. For Ahmad ibn Abi Du'ad remained a long period — forty years — debating the people of knowledge, and not one of them was able to break him. The great scholars were brought to him, the likes of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal and others among the great authorities; but they would debate him and dispute with him by way of transmitted reports — they had nothing but the statements of those who went before, "So-and-so related to us, saying, So-and-so informed us" — and he did not acknowledge this. Until al-Misisi came, and asked him only two questions. The first question: he said, "Tell me: this to which you are calling — is it something the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace), and Abu Bakr, and Umar, and Uthman, and Ali knew, or were they ignorant of it?" He said: "Rather, they knew it." He said: "Then did they call people to it?" — this is the second question — "Did they call people to it or not, or did they keep silent about it?" He said: "Rather, they kept silent about it." He said: "A thing which the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace), and Abu Bakr, and Umar, and Uthman, and Ali knew and then kept silent about — it is fitting that you should keep silent about it." So he said: "Release me from that, and the question stands as it was: rather, they were ignorant of it." He said: "A thing of which the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace), and Abu Bakr, and Umar, and Uthman, and Ali were ignorant — from where do you have knowledge of it?" Now, the question here is about the reason for the spread of the Ash'ari school in the Muslim world. I say that the Ash'ari school is the oldest of the schools of the people of the sunnah, and precedence counts for something. Then, beyond that, it is the school of most of them: it was not confined to one of the schools of law, but rather there are Hanbalis in it, and Shafi'is in it, and Malikis in it, and Hanafis in it — unlike the Maturidi school, which is confined to the scholars of the Hanafis, and the Hanbali school, which was confined to the Hanbalis in that age, or to the people of hadith along with them. This is the basic reason among the reasons for its spread. But what spread, regrettably, in the end in most countries is not the school of al-Ash'ari, but rather the positions into which the Ash'ari school was developed; and we have mentioned that the beginning of its development was with Fakhr al-Din al-Razi.

As for what concerns the contemporary sects — and in particular the Rawafid, and likewise the Ibadis, with which some countries have been afflicted — how are these people to be dealt with? Is it by suppression, and by stifling the very breath of this school until it goes away, or by disputing and debating with them? I say that the early generations had various approaches in this. Among them were those whose patience was broad enough for discussion with the people of swerving and of deviation, in the hope that God might guide them, or at the least that the proof might be established against them.

*He declines to answer, and so is not addressed, out of awe — the nobility of gravity and the might of the sovereignty of God-consciousness.*

And even in hadith: when he reported a hadith — that is, said that it had reached him from the Prophet (may God bless him and grant him peace) — no one was able to ask him about his chain of transmission for it. It is related that on one occasion Shu'bah ibn al-Hajjaj asked him, saying: "From whom did you hear this, Abu Abdallah?" He said: "I have never sat with a fool" — and he did not answer him, because he would only narrate from those whom he held to be trustworthy. But among their approaches too is the distinction between one whose return is to be hoped for — and he is the one who is fit to be called to Islam, such as the common people who follow those in error in their deviations and their errors — and one whose return is not to be hoped for. As for the one whose return is not to be hoped for: with regard to dealing with them in other respects, it is like associating with a neighbour, whoever he may be; the Muslim neighbour has two rights and the non-Muslim neighbour has one right — as the Prophet (may God bless him and grant him peace) stated explicitly. So whoever of them you hold to be an unbeliever — such as one who accuses Aisha (may God be pleased with her) of that from which God declared her innocent, and proclaims it: he is an unbeliever, and you declare him an unbeliever explicitly on account of what he said, and you deal with him as one deals with an unbelieving neighbour. For although he is not like the original unbeliever, he is an apostate unbeliever; but you are not able to carry out the prescribed penalty (ḥadd) upon him now, and that is not in your hands, so you treat him like an original unbeliever. This is especially so if he grew up in this before reaching maturity: then he is not an apostate, because he found his forefathers upon this.

As for returning the greeting of peace to those of them who are unbelievers: you do not return the greeting to him, and you do not initiate the greeting with him. And whoever you do not hold to be an unbeliever, such as their common people, you initiate the greeting with him and you return the greeting to him. As for dealing with them at work, it is not lawful to wrong them. Wrongdoing is forbidden (ḥarām) in all the revealed laws. It is not lawful to wrong the Jew, nor to wrong the Christian, nor to wrong the Rafidi, nor to wrong the deviant in any religious community whatever. So if he is a student, it is not lawful for you to withhold any part of what is his due, if he has earned it in the examination; and if he is a worker or an employee, it is not lawful for you to withhold any part of what is his due. For wrongdoing will be darknesses on the Day of Resurrection. And God, be He exalted, says — even with regard to the original polytheists.

In the Muslims' dealings with unbelievers there has always been much of the conduct of calling to Islam, which had its effect upon their souls and made many of them accept Islam and submit. Even with the Jews, they are not wronged; but in fighting them, and in their wrongdoing in that wherein they have wronged, their wrongdoing is returned upon them, and they are killed by that with which they killed. But as for one who holds a trust (amānah) or the like, he renders it to them — as the Prophet (may God bless him and grant him peace) did when the people of Mecca wronged him and drove him out in transgression and enmity and called him a liar: he rendered to them all their trusts. He left Ali behind to render their trusts to them.

flags.arabic: فمن كنت تكفره منهم ... وتعامله معاملة الجار الكافر / بالنسبة لرد السلام على الكفرة منهم، لا ترد عليه السلام ولا تبدؤه بالسلام / الروافض ... التي ابتلي بها بعض البلدان
flags.context: The final third of the tape, on how to deal with contemporary sects.
options: Withhold this record from publication pending a decision by the Sheikh's office
Publish with a prominent editorial preface setting out the context and date
Publish as translated
flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW REQUIRED (house rule 12). This passage applies the charge of unbelief to named contemporary groups, uses the pejorative al-Rawāfiḍ of the Shia, speaks of some countries being 'afflicted' with the Ibadis, withholds the greeting of peace from those judged unbelievers, and refers to the prescribed penalty for apostasy being out of reach. Read in English out of its setting — a lecture on the Islamic sciences, answering a question about the literature on sects — it carries obvious reputational and, in some jurisdictions, legal risk. It has been translated faithfully and neither softened nor strengthened. Note that the Sheikh in the same breath forbids wronging any of these groups absolutely, exempts those raised in the belief from the charge of apostasy, and directs that the greeting be exchanged with their ordinary followers; any excerpting that drops those qualifications would misrepresent him. The decision whether and how to publish belongs to Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office.

flags.arabic: والله تعالى يقول حتى في حق المشركين الأصليين.
flags.context: The closing sentence of the seventh paragraph.
options: Leave the lacuna visible, as done here
Supply the verse the Sheikh is most likely quoting
Withhold the sentence
flags.note: The Sheikh says 'And God, be He exalted, says' and the quotation that should follow is absent from the transmitted text — the sentence simply ends. The verse has NOT been restored from memory, per house rule 11; the lacuna is left visible in both the Arabic and the English. A reviewer with the audio should supply it.

flags.context: هو من رواية أبي مخلف ونوح بن أبي مريم ... اعتمد ... على أبي مخلف
options: Abu Mikhlaf, as the source spells it
Abu Mikhnaf (Lut ibn Yahya)
Leave unresolved as a transcription defect
flags.note: The transmitter whom al-Tabari, Ibn Kathir and Ibn al-Athir relied on for the reports of the first civil strife, and who is the standing example of an unacceptable narrator in this context, is Abu Mikhnaf (Lut ibn Yahya). The source spells the name مخلف in both occurrences, which is almost certainly a transcription slip in the tape. It has not been corrected in body_ar, per house rule 11; the English keeps the source's spelling and flags it here rather than substituting the expected name.

flags.context: فمنهم من كان يتسع باله لمناقشة أهل الزيغ والإلحاد لعل الله أن يهديهم
options: the people of swerving and of deviation
the people of error and of departure from the truth
the people of deviation and atheism
flags.note: ilḥād in classical usage means departing or swerving from the truth, and in this sentence it stands in parallel with zaygh and refers to members of Muslim sects whom the Sheikh hopes God may guide. Rendering it 'atheism', its ordinary modern sense, would attribute to him a claim he is not making. The classical sense has been used.

flags.arabic: يأبى الجواب فما يكلم هيبة *** شرف الوقار وعز سلطان التقى
flags.context: The line of verse stands alone between the paragraph on the approaches of the early generations and the anecdote of Shu'bah ibn al-Hajjaj.
options: Render literally and flag the missing antecedent, as done here
Withhold the line until the audio is checked
Supply the identity of the person described
flags.note: There is a lacuna here. The verse and the anecdote that follows both describe an unnamed scholar — the questioner addresses him as Abu Abdallah — but the sentence introducing him is missing from the transmitted text, so the pronoun 'he' in the following paragraph has no antecedent. The line itself also does not stand as a complete bayt: the second hemistich reads as the subject of a clause whose predicate is not present. Nothing has been supplied. A reviewer with the audio should identify the scholar and restore the missing sentence.

flags.arabic: كالسيخية الآن ... في الأصل كان أجدادهم من المسلمين، كانوا طائفة صوفية ثم انحرفوا
flags.context: The paragraph on groups that became independent religions.
options: Translate faithfully and flag, as done here
Translate with an editorial footnote on the historical question
Withhold the sentence
flags.note: The claim that Sikhism arose from a Sufi group of Muslim ancestry is contested by historians of religion and would be rejected by Sikhs themselves. It has been translated exactly as the Sheikh gives it, without correction, comment or softening, per house rule 6. It is flagged because publishing it in English, about a living religious community, is an editorial decision and not a translator's.

flags.context: ولهذا من المستحسن جدا أن يركز على المسائل المهمة في زيادة الإيمان
options: it is very much to be commended
it is strongly recommended
it is recommended (mustaḥabb)
flags.note: The word is from the same root as mustaḥabb, but here it is used evaluatively — it takes the intensifier 'very', which a formal ruling would not — and it describes what a student of the sciences would do well to concentrate on, not an act of worship. The five-rulings mapping has deliberately NOT been applied, so that no formal ruling of 'recommended' is attributed to the Sheikh on this.

flags.context: Two proper names in the fourth and fifth paragraphs.
options: Keep the source's forms and flag
Correct to al-Baghdadi and al-Misisi throughout
Leave unresolved
flags.note: The author of the well-known book on the sects is Abd al-Qahir al-Baghdadi; the source reads للبغداد, missing the final yāʾ. The interlocutor of Ahmad ibn Abi Du'ad is named first as المصيصية and then as المصيصي in the following clause. Neither has been corrected in body_ar, per house rule 11. In the English the nisbah is rendered consistently as al-Misisi and the missing letter is shown in brackets as al-Baghdad[i].

This is tape eleven of a lecture series on the Islamic religious sciences. The transmitted text begins mid-discourse, with a connective 'So…', and no opening formula; the beginning of the tape is not in the source and nothing has been supplied. The page carries no download link, and the text runs to a complete closing sentence.

The tape moves between answering audience questions and continuous exposition, and the transitions are abrupt in the source — most sharply at 'Now, the question here is about the reason for the spread of the Ash'ari school', which breaks into the middle of a paragraph. The breaks have been kept where the Arabic has them rather than smoothed over.

Positions attributed to others are kept attributed. In particular: the criticism of Ibn Taymiyyah is that the entailment of some of his statements runs against his own position and can be read as the view of the Nawasib, while the Sheikh expressly says he did not intend this and asks God's protection for him. That qualification is part of the judgement and must not be dropped.

naṣb, rendered 'hostility to Ali and his house', and al-Nawāṣib, 'the Nawasib', are the creedal terms for the position opposed to that of the Shia. They are left transliterated because no English equivalent carries the sectarian reference.
'The people of the sunnah' renders ahl al-sunnah throughout; 'the early generations' renders al-salaf.

The Sheikh refers to 'the civil strife' (al-fitnah) without further specification; the reference is to the conflict among the Companions after the killing of Uthman, as the names Talhah, al-Zubayr and Aisha indicate. No explanatory expansion has been inserted into the text.
